_review: DRAFT for the user's review (story: Claude drafts, the user reviews). Every line of text here is a proposal. Rewritten 2026-10-09: quests built on gameplay (fights in waves, an escort, a practice pillar, Echo-stone gestures, a carried flame, Run medals), with consequences in the Warden fight.
title: The Snow That Would Not Fall

npcs.name: Aud
npcs.about: The last keeper of the monastery. Swept the floor around the Shaper's body for nine winters.

npcs.name: Old Maren
npcs.about: Leads the pilgrims. Remembers snow that fell.

npcs.name: Tobin
npcs.about: A pilgrim child who follows things.

npcs.name: Isolde
npcs.about: Keeps the camp's lantern. Plays the lyre at night.

npcs.name: Varo
npcs.about: A staff-bearer who walked out to watch the Warden and did not come back.

aud.wake.speaker: aud
lines: You stood up out of his robe.
Nine winters I swept around him. I thought the cloth would rot before it moved.
The hall's three stones still remember a Shaper's hands. Give one its gesture back: freeze it, sweep it or pour the ribbon onto it.
Go carefully when you do. Something has been listening at the bottom of the steps.

aud.cloister.speaker: aud
lines: So they come up the steps now. They never did, while he lay here.
Rest at the shrine by the east wall. If you fall, that is where you will stand up again.
Then take the Run down to the pilgrims' fire. The Shapers went that way. Lean, and the slope will carry you.

aud.go.speaker: aud
lines: The shrine, then the Run. Lean into it. The slope remembers how they rode it.

aud.again.speaker: aud
lines: The stones first. They have waited longer than I have.

aud.after.speaker: aud
lines: I heard snow land on the roof this morning. I had forgotten that it makes a sound.
Ring the bell for me. My arms are too old, and it should be rung by the one who did this.

aud.bell.speaker: aud
lines: Nine winters it hung there. Now it will not stop humming. Neither will I.

maren.raid.speaker: maren
lines: Not now — the hounds! Drive them off the fire, and then we will talk.

maren.first.speaker: maren
lines: You came down the Run like the stories said, and you came down fighting. Good.
Out past the watching stone something old lies across the steppe and holds the snow in the air. A Warden.
Varo went to watch it, and the hounds have him pinned at his stone. The boy has wandered again; small tracks, west to the spring.
And a sled went out to the east ridge for wood yesterday. It has not come back. Isolde has her own errand, for the dark hours.
Sleep by our fire when you need to. If you fall out there, you will wake beside it.

maren.again.speaker: maren
lines: Varo first. He is stubborn, but he is not foolish, and he has watched that thing longer than anyone.

maren.sled.speaker: maren
lines: Torn felt and no driver. Follow the prints to the ridge, then. And if what made them is bigger than a hound, come back and tell me.

maren.tobin.speaker: maren
lines: You brought him back. He says you walk without a sound and he had to listen for you.
Take this. It was a Shaper's before it was ours, and it never fit any of our hands.

maren.hounds.speaker: maren
lines: An old one, in the den? Then that is why they kept coming. She was feeding them.
The children walked to the water-hole this morning and no one followed them. If the Warden calls its Shaped to it, fewer will come now.

maren.night.speaker: maren
lines: My mother saw them once. Tall, robed like you. They walked ahead of the weather.
Where they stopped, the snow came down. Where they went on, it followed.

maren.after.speaker: maren
lines: Listen. Snow is falling on the tents. I am too old to cry about weather, and I am crying about weather.
Aud will want the bell rung. Go up, before the snow fills the Run.

tobin.found.speaker: tobin
lines: They went away. Were they yours? They didn't look like anybody's.
There's water under the ice. It's not moving either. But it's talking, if you're quiet.
I'm not lost. I was following the quiet.

options.text: Lead him back to the fire.
Let him listen a while longer.

tobin.walking.speaker: tobin
lines: Your feet don't make the same sound mine do. They don't make any.

tobin.listening.speaker: tobin
lines: It's singing about the big ridge. There are lots of voices, up on stone posts, and one of them is cracked. You can hear it if you listen.
The cracked one will break first. I think it wants to.

tobin.again.speaker: tobin
lines: Do you have a face in there? Maren says no. I think it's just dark.

tobin.after.speaker: tobin
lines: The spring is talking now. It doesn't say anything. It just talks.

isolde.day.speaker: isolde
lines: The lantern was lit at the monastery, nine winters ago. I carry it so the fire never has to start from nothing.
There are braziers by three of the shrines, and one at the edge of the Warden's ground. Cold since the snow stopped falling.
Come back after dark. I will put the flame in your lantern, if you can keep it alive that far.

isolde.flame.speaker: isolde
lines: Hold the lantern still. There.
Walk, don't run. Don't let anything strike you, and don't stand in the snow longer than you must. It is an old flame; it tires.
And it will be seen. Things that are cold come to look at warm things.

isolde.relight.speaker: isolde
lines: Gone out? It does that. It went out on me twice in the first winter. Hold still.

isolde.night.speaker: isolde
lines: Sit, if you sit. I only know the slow songs. The fast ones need wind.

isolde.song.speaker: isolde
lines: Four flames, and all of them leaning the same way. Sit.
This one is older than the camp. It is about a stone that listens, past the far ridge, and another below the tarn. I never went.

isolde.after.speaker: isolde
lines: The flame leans now. I had never seen it lean.

varo.first.speaker: varo
lines: Good. I was running out of ways to be still. Do you see it? I thought it was a ridge for three days.
When it wakes, pillars come up out of the snow round it with crystals on them. The crystals feed it. You cannot hurt it while they stand.
And when it stops moving and lifts its head, it is not resting. It throws its spines, everywhere, at once. Nothing stops them but stone.
There is a small one here, a seedling, by my stone. Learn on that one. Climb it, break it, and when it stills, put my stone between you.

varo.again.speaker: varo
lines: The seedling. Climb, break, and get behind the stone when it brightens. Better to learn it here than out there.

varo.seedling.speaker: varo
lines: You hid well. Most things that live out here learned to hide the hard way.
Six pillars round the big one. Break them all, then its seams: freeze them, then break them. Take this; it will hold the ice in its joints a little longer.

varo.ready.speaker: varo
lines: Six crystals, then its seams. And stone between you whenever it stills.

varo.after.speaker: varo
lines: It is a hill now. A good hill. I will tell them it lay down on its own; they would not believe the rest.
Far below, a long white ridge breathes once, slowly, and is still.
Far off, the first snow in nine winters reaches the ground.
The note goes out over the steppe, and the snow carries it a long way.

maren.early.speaker: maren
lines: A robe with no one in it. Stand by the fire, then; the hounds have been circling us since dusk, and they will come again.

quests.title: The Empty Robe
quests.summary: Something has woken in the last Shaper's robe.

steps.journal: I woke in the monastery where the last Shaper died. A keeper named Aud was waiting.
The hall's three stones remember a Shaper's hands. Cast a stone's own gesture onto it — Crystallize, Sweep or Ribbon.
The stone woke something at the bottom of the steps. Shaped, rising out of the snow.
Aud: rest at the shrine by the east wall. If I fall, I will stand up there.
The Shapers' Run falls from the shoulder to the pilgrims' plain: nine gates, one long slope. Hold right mouse to surf it.

optional.journal: Wake all three of the hall's stones.
Something lies across the plain below the Run.

quests.title: The Pilgrims' Fire
quests.summary: Hounds have come down on the last pilgrims' camp.

steps.journal: The Shaped are at the pilgrims' fire. Drive them off before they reach the tents.
The fire is safe. Old Maren leads the pilgrims; she will know why the snow hangs.

quests.title: The Watching Stone
quests.summary: A staff-bearer went out to watch the Warden and was trapped there.

steps.journal: Hounds have Varo pinned at his watching stone, east of the fire. Break them.
Varo is free. He has watched the Warden longer than anyone.
Varo: a seedling pillar stands by his stone. Climb it (hold right mouse at its foot), break its crystal, and when it stills and brightens, put the stone between us.
The seedling is broken. Varo saw it.

quests.title: The Held Snow
quests.summary: A Warden lies across the steppe, holding its snow in the air.

steps.journal: When it wakes, six pillars rise round it, a crystal healing it from each. Climb them and break them; then freeze its seams and break them, and wear it down. When it stills and lifts its head, get behind stone. If I fall, it lies down again and waits.

quests.title: First Snow
quests.summary: The Warden has lain down. Motion is returning to the steppe.

steps.journal: The snow is falling again. The pilgrims should see it.
Snow on the tents. Maren is waiting by the fire.
Aud asked that the monastery bell be rung when the snow fell again, by the one who brought it down.

quests.title: A Trail in the Snow
quests.summary: A pilgrim child has wandered from the fire.

steps.journal: Small footprints lead west across the frozen tarn. Follow them.
Tobin is out on the spring's ice, and two hounds are circling it.
The hounds are gone. Tobin is still listening to the ice.
Lead Tobin back to the fire (he follows, if I do not leave him behind) — or leave him listening.

optional.journal: When the steppe moves again, come back to the spring.

quests.title: The Den Mother
quests.summary: A wood sled went out to the east ridge and did not come back.

steps.journal: Maren: a sled went east toward the ridge for wood. Find it.
Hound prints, many, from the wreck up to the ridge. Follow them to the den and break what lives there.
The den is empty. Maren will want to know what was in it.

quests.title: Echoes of the Shapers
quests.summary: Echo stones stand hidden across the steppe. Each remembers a Shaper's gesture.

steps.journal: Echo stones answer only up close. Listen at one, and give it back the gesture it remembers. Three of them.
Three have answered. The rest stand farther out, higher up.

optional.journal: Rest at all five shrines on the steppe.

quests.title: Carry the Flame
quests.summary: Isolde keeps the last flame from the monastery. The braziers have been cold for nine winters.

steps.journal: Isolde will light my lantern from hers, after dark.
Carry the flame to the four cold braziers — three by the shrines, one at the edge of the Warden's ground. It gutters if I hurry and dies if I am struck. If it dies, Isolde will light it again.
All four burn, leaning one way. Isolde will play, after dark.

quests.title: The Shapers' Run
quests.summary: The Shapers rode the long chute faster than anyone has since.

steps.journal: Ride all nine gates in under 48 seconds.
Under 40 seconds.
Under 34 seconds — the way they rode it.

echo-frost-hold.name: Echo of the Held Breath
echo-frost-hold.effect: Frozen joints and Shaped stay frozen 40% longer.
echo-frost-hold.text: What is held may be held a little longer.

echo-frost-surf.name: Echo of the Running Water
echo-frost-surf.effect: Snow-surf keeps its speed longer on flats.
echo-frost-surf.text: Water remembers which way is down.

echo-frost-still.name: Echo of the Still Stone
echo-frost-still.effect: Focus returns faster while standing still.
echo-frost-still.text: The stones were patient. So were they.

echo-frost-sweep.name: Echo of the Open Hand
echo-frost-sweep.text: The hand remembers how far it went.

lore-shapers-walked.title: They Walked Ahead of the Weather
lore-shapers-walked.text: The Shapers did not command the snow. They walked, and the snow came after, the way a dog follows someone it loves. — as told by Old Maren

lore-spring.title: The Sleeping Spring
lore-spring.text: Beneath the ice the water stands in the shape it had when the last Shaper died, mid-ripple, waiting to finish the motion.

lore-five-stones.title: The Five Stones
lore-five-stones.text: Each shrine marks where a Shaper stood still for a night. It was the only stillness they allowed themselves. The stones kept it for them.

lore-slow-songs.title: The Slow Songs
lore-slow-songs.text: Pilgrims' songs lost their quick verses as the wind died. Isolde says the quick verses were about weather, and no one could remember what weather sounded like.

lore-shapers-run.title: The Shapers' Run
lore-shapers-run.text: The first Shapers did not walk down from the monastery. They leaned, and the snow took them, and the slope was cut afterward to match.

lore-spring-voice.title: What Tobin Heard
lore-spring-voice.text: Under the ice, the spring says a single word, over and over. Tobin will not say it. He says it is not for people.

lore-stones-heard.title: Six Voices
lore-stones-heard.text: Six stones, six Shapers who stopped to speak where no one would pass. Together they say: we left the snow to you.

lore-hounds.title: The Den Mother
lore-hounds.text: The Shaped are what a stilled place dreams of itself: hungry because everything is still, quick because nothing else is. The old ones grow a rime that turns blows aside; cold is the only thing that reaches them.

lore-echo-frost-1.title: Echo Stone 1
lore-echo-frost-1.text: The first Shaper stood here to see how far the steppe went. It went further.

lore-echo-frost-2.title: Echo Stone 2
lore-echo-frost-2.text: Do not trust a calm slope. Trust the one that leans.

lore-echo-frost-3.title: Echo Stone 3
lore-echo-frost-3.text: I buried my name here. Not because it was shameful. It was heavy.

lore-echo-frost-4.title: Echo Stone 4
lore-echo-frost-4.text: The water under the tarn counted my steps. I stopped at one hundred and one.

lore-echo-frost-5.title: Echo Stone 5
lore-echo-frost-5.text: Where the wind turns, I turned. It made me kinder.

lore-echo-frost-6.title: Echo Stone 6
lore-echo-frost-6.text: The last of us wrote nothing. This stone is the note.

lore-bell.title: The Bell
lore-bell.text: The bell was cast to be rung once each winter, when the first snow reached the monastery steps. It was rung for the last time the winter before the last Shaper died, and then it hung, waiting, with the snow.

barks._comment: Ambient lines a Veiled says as the Wraith passes (systems/barks.js): the first entry whose `when` matches, one per NPC every ~2 minutes. DRAFT for the user's review.

lines: The wind is in the cloister again. I keep stopping to listen to it.
Nine winters of sweeping, and now the snow comes in faster than I can.
The steps are clear. Go on; the bier will keep.
It wore that robe for sixty years. It never once ran.
Mind the floor. It remembers footsteps.
Still here. The robe is still here.
Snow on my hood. I had forgotten the weight of it.
The children are trying to catch it on their tongues. Let them.
Behind the fire, all of you!
Not the tents — keep them from the tents!
Sit, if a robe can sit. The fire is for anyone.
Count the tents for me. My eyes go first at night.
We came for the Shaper. We stayed for the quiet.
Old knees, old snow. Neither moves.
Is it far? It feels far.
I can walk. I just walk slow.
I told them you'd find me. Nobody believed me.
Can I follow you again? Not far. Just to the stones.
Your hands are cold even from here.
Maren says not to stare. I'm not staring. I'm looking.
Keep it out of the wind. And out of a hurry.
It burns smaller in your hand than in mine. That's all right.
The lyre's out of tune with the cold. I play it anyway.
Every lantern is a little promise, you know.
I trim the wick every hour. Old habit, from when the wind still blew it out.
Light travels a long way here. Further than voices.
It's lying down. I watched it for three years and it never once lay down.
I could walk home now. I think I'll stand a little longer.
Watch the spires on its back. They burn before it breaks loose.
Stone stops it. Nothing else I've seen does.
Don't wave. It sees movement.
Down there. The white ridge that isn't a ridge.
